quickSummary: The Endomembrane System comprises organelles coordinated by vesicular transport (ER, Golgi, Lysosomes, Vacuoles; excludes Mitochondria, Plastids, and Peroxisomes). RER bears 80S ribosomes anchored by Ribophorins (protein synthesis and N-glycosylation). SER synthesizes lipids/steroids, detoxifies drugs via Cytochrome P450, and stores Ca2+ in sarcoplasmic reticulum. Golgi has cis (forming) and trans (maturing) faces, mediating O-glycosylation, cell plate synthesis, and acrosome formation via COP II (anterograde), COP I (retrograde), and Clathrin coats.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Endomembrane System = ER + Golgi + Lysosomes + Vacuoles. Mitochondria, Plastids, and Peroxisomes are strictly EXCLUDED because their functions are uncoordinated with vesicular trafficking.

conceptBreakdown.content: The Endomembrane System comprises eukaryotic membrane-bound organelles whose physiological functions are tightly coordinated through vesicular trafficking.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER vs SER)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER vs SER)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ROUGH ER vs SMOOTH ER
                      
   ROUGH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (RER)       SMOOTH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (SER)
   ├── Studded with 80S Ribosomes          ├── Lacks Ribosomes
   ├── Bound via **Ribophorin I & II**     ├── Tubular membrane network
   ├── Site of Protein Synthesis,          ├── Site of **Lipid / Steroid Synthesis**
   │   folding, & N-linked Glycosylation   │   (cholesterol, estrogen, testosterone)
   └── Abundant in pancreatic acinar cells └── Detoxification via **Cytochrome P450**;
                                               stores $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum**
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**: Flattened cisternae studded with 80S ribosomes anchored via glycoprotein receptors **Ribophorin I and Ribophorin II**. Site of secretory protein synthesis, folding, and core **N-linked glycosylation**.
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)**: Interconnected tubular network lacking ribosomes. Functions:
  1. **Lipid and Steroid Hormone Synthesis** (cholesterol, phospholipids, estrogens, androgens).
  2. **Drug and Toxin Detoxification** via **Cytochrome P450** monooxygenases in hepatocytes.
  3. **Calcium Storage & Release**: Specialized as the **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum** in skeletal muscle cells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Golgi Apparatus & Vesicle Coat Proteins
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Golgi Apparatus & Vesicle Coat Proteins
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VESICLE COAT PROTEINS
                          
   COP II: Anterograde Transport ──► Endoplasmic Reticulum ──► Cis-Golgi
   COP I:  Retrograde Transport  ──► Cis-Golgi ─────────────► Endoplasmic Reticulum
   CLATHRIN: Trans-Golgi Target  ──► Trans-Golgi ───────────► Lysosomes / Endosomes
conceptBreakdown.content:
Consists of parallel curved flattened cisternae exhibiting distinct morphological polarity:
• **Cis Face (Forming / Convex Face)**: Oriented toward the ER; receives incoming transport vesicles.
• **Trans Face (Maturing / Concave Face)**: Oriented toward the plasma membrane; buds off processed secretory vesicles and lysosomes.

### Primary Golgi Functions
1. **Post-Translational Modification**: Directs **O-linked glycosylation** of proteins and lipids into glycoproteins and glycolipids.
2. **Cell Wall Matrix Synthesis**: Synthesizes non-cellulosic polysaccharides (pectin, hemicellulose) assembled into the **cell plate (phragmoplast)** during plant cytokinesis.
3. **Acrosome Biogenesis**: Packages hydrolytic enzymes to form the sperm **Acrosome** cap.
